name: Andrology and men's reproductive health
summary: How expats find andrology and male reproductive health care in Singapore for fertility workups, hypogonadism questions, and sexual health — coordinated with IVF clinics and urology when needed.
body:
Andrology focuses on male fertility and reproductive endocrinology: semen analysis interpretation, varicoceles, hormone issues, and medical optimisation before IVF/ICSI. General urology covers surgical anatomy; fertility-focused andrology sits closer to reproductive medicine teams.

## Common entry points
- Couple fertility workup after 6–12 months of trying (or sooner with known risk factors)
- Abnormal semen analysis needing repeat testing and lifestyle/medical review
- Prior chemotherapy, undescended testis history, or genetic concerns
- Hypogonadism symptoms — careful distinction from wellness “testosterone package” marketing
- Sexual health issues needing medical rather than spa-clinic framing

## IVF coordination
Many couples meet andrology through a fertility centre. Ask how semen processing, surgical sperm retrieval, and genetic counselling are handled in one pathway. Parallel GP testosterone ads rarely belong in a fertility plan without proper labs and shared decision-making.

## How to choose
Prefer clinicians linked to accredited fertility or urology departments who explain evidence for supplements vs procedures. Confirm lab accreditation for semen analysis — collection timing and abstinence windows change results. Insurance often excludes fertility; get cash estimates early.

## Practical tip
Repeat an abnormal semen analysis before invasive steps — one hot Grab ride or recent fever can skew results. Bring overseas labs with reference ranges; units differ across countries.
whenToEngage: Couple fertility workup needs male-factor assessment
Abnormal semen analysis needs specialist interpretation
Considering surgical sperm retrieval with IVF clinic
Wellness testosterone package before proper hormone workup
